assessments.reasoning: I opened the retained original PDF. Its complete digest and all four proposed span digests matched enrollment. Both full-page headers identify N3220 as a working draft. PDF page 52, printed page 39, places the arithmetic rule in §6.2.5 ¶11. The crop shows a baseline 2 with N raised to its upper right in the modulus. Earlier in the same paragraph, the minus sign and 1 sit on the baseline after 2 with raised N, giving the inclusive upper bound 2^N − 1. PDF page 55, printed page 42, places the width definition in §6.2.6.2 ¶1. Its crop distinguishes the highest value-bit weight, 2^(N−1), with the entire N−1 raised, from the maximum value, 2^N − 1. The paragraph identifies N as the count of value bits and treats padding separately. Together the two passages establish the claimed modulus and the meaning of its exponent for arithmetic performed in the unsigned type. The conclusion is descriptive of this draft and makes no finding about a particular compiler.

challenge.method: Tested whether flattening the formulas could change the modulus, whether padding could increase N, and whether an unsigned operand alone brings an expression within scope. Inspected the other two proposed byte ranges for substantive evidence.
challenge.results: The glyph positions distinguish all three formulas. Padding contributes no value bits. An operation performed in signed int after promotion falls outside the claim, even if an operand began with unsigned type. Conversions serve only to delimit applicability here. The other two ranges contain PDF reference metadata and were omitted from the citation.

limitations: The rule describes the named working draft and does not assert modulo arithmetic for signed calculations or imply behavior for a particular compiler.
The result describes unsigned integer arithmetic in N3220. Effective type after conversions, signed arithmetic, and implementation behavior have their own rules.
